Emergency personnel and crews are on the scene after a tanker crashed into a river cruise boat in New Orleans on November 13, 2026 [Matthew Hinton/AP]By Al Jazeera Staff and The Associated PressPublished On 13 Nov 202613 Nov 2026
A tanker has struck a river cruise boat carrying 129 passengers on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, partially submerging the vessel and prompting a major rescue operation.
The Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the American Heritage paddleboat on Friday at about 12:30pm local time (18:30 GMT), the Port of New Orleans said. The cruise boat had docked about two hours earlier to begin letting passengers off. The authorities have not released any information on injuries or deaths.

“Multiple individuals have been rescued, and search-and-rescue operations remain ongoing,” a city spokesperson said.
Video from the scene showed the much larger tanker hitting the paddlewheel cruise boat as metal and glass crashed and crunched, according to The Associated Press news agency.
More than a dozen people in life jackets were dragged from the river, where the water temperature was 19 degrees Celsius (66 degrees Fahrenheit), onto nearby ships, while others stood near the railing as the boat listed further into the water.

An American Airlines commercial aircraft approaches to land at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, as seen from the Lincoln Memorial at the National Mall, Washington, DC, US, on November 2, 2026 [Umit Bektas/Reuters]By ReutersPublished On 13 Nov 202613 Nov 2026
The United States has grounded flights across the country after a “communication issue” impacted traffic control centres, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.
“FAA [Federal Aviation Administration] technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them,” Duffy wrote on social media.
The FAA said in a post on X that there had been a “temporary telecommunications outage” and that, as a precaution, all flights were being halted. International flights would be handled case by case, it added.
About 7,000 flights have been either delayed or cancelled due to the stop, according to FlightAware.
Some 4,042 flights were in the air, heading to US airports, when the ground stop was ordered, according to the tracking site Flightradar24.
The communication issue affects all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which guide aircraft.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters there was no indication that the ground stop was triggered by a threat to the US. “Everybody’s safe. The flights are accounted for,” he said. “This is not another 9/11.”
President Donald Trump had been briefed, he said.
Asked whether a planned rollout of a new AI tool meant to help air traffic controllers could be to blame, Mullin said officials had not ruled it out. “You just can’t rule out anything at this point. We are going through that process,” he said.

Faithful attend a mass celebrated by Pope Leo XIV at the Pampas de Pimentel esplanade, in Pimentel, near Chiclayo, Peru, November 13, 2026 [Paolo Aguilar/EPA]By Al Jazeera Staff, Reuters and The Associated PressPublished On 13 Nov 202613 Nov 2026
Pope Leo has made an emotional return to his former diocese of Chiclayo in Peru, where large crowds welcomed their former bishop exactly one month after he had lung cancer surgery, and he thanked them for their support during his recovery.
“As I look at your faces, a prayer of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life,” he said.

About 500,000 people gathered for Mass at Pampas de Pimentel, a desert park just outside of Peru’s fourth-largest city, according to estimates from the Vatican, while another million lined his motorcade route.
Before he was elected pope, Leo had spent about two decades working in Peru as a missionary priest and served as bishop of Chiclayo, where he is still known as “Padre Roberto” and where his image is ubiquitous, from 2015 to 2023.
In Chiclayo, a coastal city of about 620,000, Leo earned a reputation for staying close to poor communities during times of crisis, including when the region was hit with devastating floods and the COVID-19 pandemic.

Paraguay's former President Santiago Pena (L) arrives at the Attorney General's Office to appear before prosecutors, a day after he was impeached and placed under house arrest amid a political and financial crisis triggered by the collapse of digital lender Ueno, in Asuncion, Paraguay, November 7, 2026 [Fiscalia Paraguay/Handout via Reuters]By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and ReutersPublished On 13 Nov 202613 Nov 2026
Paraguayan prosecutors have charged former president Santiago Pena with criminal association over his alleged role in the collapse of the digital bank Ueno, a week after Congress removed him from office.
The prosecutor’s office announced the new charge on Friday, adding to the breach of trust and self-dealing charges already facing Pena, who is being held in pretrial detention at a military facility.
Recommended Stories list of 1 itemlist 1 of 1Paraguay’s ousted president charged over banking scandalend of list
The 47-year-old former leader is accused of using his position to direct millions in government funds to Ueno and concealing or downplaying its financial troubles, despite warnings of risky lending practices, while having financial ties to the bank.
He denies all charges.
Pena, who entered office in 2023, held a stake in the bank’s holding company until last year.
On Thursday, investigators raided his official residence in the capital, Asuncion. The prosecutor’s office said agents from the economic crimes unit were extracting data and gathering relevant information for the investigation.
Last week, Pena tried to step down as president, but Congress rejected his resignation, instead removing him from office through impeachment. Pena was arrested shortly after his removal.

Microsoft has said its popular email and other services were improving but not fully restored more than 24 hours after a mass outage disrupted communications worldwide.
The outage, which began around 16:00 GMT on Thursday and affected users in 74 countries, was caused by overloaded servers that became “unexpectedly available,” the company reported. There was no indication of a cyberattack or malicious activity, the tech giant said on Friday.

“We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure,” the company said in a statement.
Microsoft reported that “email queues [are] significantly reduced and approaching normal levels”.
The outage affected Microsoft 365 services used by global businesses, institutions and individuals, including Outlook, Teams and Copilot, its artificial intelligence (AI) tool. It was one of the longest in Microsoft’s history and the second disruption to its services this year.
While Microsoft has not said how many people were affected by the outage, the company announced in January that it had more than 450 million Microsoft 365 commercial subscribers. The United States-based tech giant is valued at more than $3.8 trillion.

Nigerian health authorities say they have completed a 21-day monitoring period for the 62 contacts of a person who contracted the Ebola virus, ⁠⁠with none of them falling ill.
Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on October 20 in a Swiss woman who had travelled to Uganda and then returned ‌‌to Nigeria.

The patient and her husband were evacuated to Switzerland where she recovered fully and has been discharged from hospital.
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said on Friday that none of the 62 contacts identified after the first case have developed the disease, with the ⁠⁠last contact just discharged.
Thirteen ⁠⁠contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during monitoring, but all of them tested negative for the virus, the NCDC said.
⁠The agency added, however, that completing contact monitoring does not by itself mean the outbreak is over.
According to World Health Organization (WHO) protocols, ‌‌a country must complete a full 42-day countdown from the recovery or departure of the last confirmed ‌‌patient ‌‌before an official end-of-outbreak declaration can be made.
